text.paragraph: Primary care visit for four months of tiredness, breathlessness, sore tongue, and tingling feet, with long-standing low back pain. Concerns: Four months of tiredness, breathlessness on stairs, a sore tongue, and tingling in both feet, with unsteadiness in the dark; Low back pain for many years since a train collision and a car crash, worse after standing at the range. tr.td: Physical therapy program for chronic low back pain: eight weekly sessions of supervised exercise, core and hip strengthening, and balance training, with a home program

Esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsies of the gastric body, antrum, and incisura in separate jars, and of the duodenum: pale, thin corpus mucosa with visible vessels and loss of folds; two 3 mm body polyps removed (hyperplastic). Histology: corpus-predominant atrophic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia and linear ECL-cell hyperplasia, antrum spared; no neuroendocrine tumor, dysplasia, or cancer; H. pylori negative; duodenal villi normal
Colonoscopy to the cecum for iron deficiency: a few sigmoid diverticula; no polyps, tumor, or bleeding source

tr.td: Intramuscular cyanocobalamin 1000 micrograms daily for one week, weekly for four weeks, then monthly for life
Hematology consultation to confirm pernicious anemia, review the cytopenias and neurologic findings, and advise on replacement and gastric risk

Monitor the response on the CMID schedule: reticulocytes at one week, potassium during early replacement, blood count and MMA at eight weeks, and a neurologic examination at each visit; no routine repeat B12 level

Upper endoscopy with topographic gastric biopsies to confirm autoimmune gastritis and look for neuroendocrine tumors and gastric neoplasia, with H. pylori testing and TSH for autoimmune thyroid disease
Treat iron deficiency unmasked by recovery with alternate-day oral iron, and complete the GI evaluation with colonoscopy
Chronic low back pain: eight weeks of supervised exercise therapy and a home program, heat, and tai chi; an NSAID as needed once the platelet count is normal; no imaging without red flags
Fall prevention: neuropathy and gait checks at each visit, strength and balance exercise, night lights, and home-safety review
Normal hemoglobin and MCV within eight weeks of starting B12 replacement
Hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL and MCV 96 fL at eight weeks
Stop the progression of neuropathy and recover balance, with no falls
Paresthesia gone, Romberg negative, vibration mildly reduced at the great toes only; no falls
Reduce back pain to 3 of 10 or less and the Oswestry score below 20 percent by the five-month review
Return to teaching full shooting classes
Teaching two full classes a week
